wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Talks in New York on reopening Hormuz saw Trump reject Iran's proposal, while UK police probed a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, a base used by the US; Iran denied any link. Mediation then deadlocked and the Pentagon drafted strike options, but Iran agreed safe Hormuz lanes with Oman and Pezeshkian says it will keep negotiating.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light crude pumped from the North Sea, and the reference against which most of the world's traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel, freight and inflation in importing countries follow it.
brent.recent: The war around the Strait of Hormuz choked the route tankers use: seven ships crossed on Tuesday, the fewest since 23 July, and projectiles hit a tanker off Qatar. Houthi missiles struck Riyadh's airport on two straight days, and the Pentagon drafted Iran strike options. Delta put its extra fuel bill at $6 billion.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate is the light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for oil produced in the United States. American petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do the budgets of shale producers.
wti.recent: The war around the Strait of Hormuz choked Middle East shipments and put a war premium on every barrel. That premium eased as the region's crude exports climbed back past pre-war levels, the G7 released stocks and Saudi Arabia unexpectedly cut its prices to Asia; Kuwait still pumps only about 75% of its prewar oil.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at Henry Hub, a pipeline junction in Louisiana, and the benchmark for US gas. Power plants, home heating and LNG export contracts are priced off it, so it moves on weather and storage.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas story was LNG at the Strait of Hormuz, not US supply: more Qatari tankers cleared it, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it struck a gas tanker there, and Pakistan sought 22 winter gas cargoes but may get 12. None of that accounts for the price at Henry Hub.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat, a benchmark for the world's most traded bread grain. Importers across North Africa and South Asia buy against it, and the cost of flour and subsidised bread follows.
wheat.recent: Sindh will sell state wheat to flour mills below the market from 15 October to hold down flour prices, while Islamabad has yet to set the support price growers need before sowing starts. Egypt delayed a second bread price request in months. None of this accounts for the rise in the world price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the reference grade for world trade. Rice feeds more than half of humanity, and a handful of Asian exporters set what importers in Africa and the Middle East pay.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, the weakest since 2015, while floods killed at least 62 in Uttar Pradesh and Bangkok had its worst flooding in 15 years. All of it came after this monthly series was last published, so none of it accounts for the fall shown.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in wiring, motors and power grids. Chile and Peru mine much of it and China buys about half, so it moves with construction, electrification and mine stoppages.
copper.recent: Two unions at Chile's Centinela mine decided to strike, and China is demanding copper supply guarantees as its condition for approving the Anglo Teck merger, three sources say. Both came after this monthly series' last reading, so neither accounts for the climb it shows.

us-10y.standing: The interest the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other countries' borrowing costs are priced off it, so it carries Fed policy into the wider economy.
us-10y.recent: Oil is behind it: Brent neared $110 a barrel, and with US inflation above the Fed's target for 5.5 years, most Federal Reserve officials expect another rate hike by year-end. The sell-off is global — Japan's 10-year yield neared a 30-year high and the ECB hiked last month — while Washington pays about $1 trillion a year in interest.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The fortnight's news ran against the index rather than with it: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over private credit, US bond yields kept rising, and the war around Hormuz held Brent crude above $100. None of it accounts for the price.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants carry most of that weight, so it moves with what investors pay for big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The slip from the peak followed Washington suspending Microsoft and Adobe from a visa programme over fraud claims; Microsoft, one of the index's heaviest members, fell 7.5%. Before that, a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits against Google, and the top tech firms signed an accord with Trump to self-police AI.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The war around the Strait of Hormuz has kept Brent crude above $100, and crude is most of what a gallon costs. States cut fuel taxes weeks before the midterms, the International Energy Agency released 100 million barrels of oil and fuel, and Washington licensed Russian diesel to bring prices down.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub, and the benchmark for European gas contracts. Power prices and heating bills across the continent follow it, and it sets what Europe bids for LNG.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatari LNG tankers are clearing Hormuz in growing numbers despite attacks on shipping, Dmitriev offered to reopen Nord Stream jointly, and wind and solar spared the UK more than 100 LNG tanker deliveries. All of that came after the months charted here, and none of it accounts for the price.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: US 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2002 in early October, a strain in the bond market that did not carry into what traders pay for protection on shares. Nothing else reported in the fortnight accounts for the index.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan reviewed a fuel subsidy that 7.6 million riders have registered for, the IMF argued that such subsidies cost 3-6 times more than targeted cash, and the army confirmed troops in Saudi Arabia. None of it accounts for the rupee's path.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria's news this fortnight was about public money, not the exchange rate: auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at the central bank, and the state oil company lost 77.6% of its fuel-products revenue. Petrol rose from ₦830 to ₦1,400 a litre since February. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight's news from Cairo was the arrest of all 6 Matsda2sh journalists and a year's postponement of Egypt's criminal procedures code. None of it touches trade, borrowing or monetary policy, and nothing here accounts for the pound's move.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: Turkey pledged with Pakistan to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia as Houthi drone attacks on Riyadh escalated, Ukraine said a Russian drone attack sank a ship in the Black Sea, and Moscow floated letting Turkey move its S-400s. These are security stories; none is a monetary or trade event that accounts for the rate.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The news from Bangladesh in these weeks was political rather than monetary: a foreign policy being redrawn away from New Delhi, an envoy's account of Sheikh Hasina's arrival in India, and mob violence testing the country's institutions. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The news from Indonesia in these weeks was a new finance minister facing a test of delivery, a prison scandal in Cibinong and an MSCI rating of Chinese mining firms. None of it accounts for the rupiah's move.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The news from Lebanon in these weeks was about security rather than money: an Israeli minister, Smotrich, called for annexation of Lebanon, and Israel pressed for a US-led force to disarm Hezbollah. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The EU pressed Beijing over the yuan as its 2025 deficit with China reached 360.6 billion euros, and China rejected the charges; the two sides then agreed an interim deal limiting China's hybrid car exports. Beijing also freed 550 billion yuan of unused local borrowing room, a fiscal step. None of it accounts for the rate's drift.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The RBI raised its repo rate to 5.5%, the first rise since 2023, a move forced by Hormuz and mounting inflation risks, and the rupee weakened anyway. The Sensex fell for a seventh week over oil and Iran, and the government confirmed that banks have paid a 3% tax on gold imports since April, a step meant to curb imports and protect the currency.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real's weak point came two days before the vote: the final debate was cancelled over a bomb scare, the US and Australia shut consular services, and the Banco Master collapse hung over the race. It firmed once Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and his potential finance chief called for a fast fiscal fix.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's news from Mexico was about storms and security, not the economy: Hurricane Polo made landfall twice on the Pacific coast, 500 US troops deployed over a border shooting Mexico cannot verify, and a prison fight in Mazatlán killed 10. None of it accounts for the peso's move.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The ECB raised rates in September and later called the step proportionate, as euro-zone inflation jumped to 3.8% from 3.2% and business activity reached a 3½-year high. A hike and faster growth ordinarily lift a currency, so none of that accounts for a euro that lost ground to the dollar.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources said the Bank of Japan may declare its 2% inflation goal reached. Higher yields and a central bank closer to tightening normally lift a currency, so neither accounts for the yen's slide.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the rate. The one story touching Russia's export earnings: Trump said after a call with Putin that the United States will take Russian diesel, and Alexander Novak promised 300,000 tonnes this month. Ukrainian drones hit a crude tanker off Sochi and two Yandex data centres.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's fortnight was domestic and political: Home Affairs withdrew an asylum directive after riots in Durban and Soweto, gunmen killed 17 in a bar shooting, and Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize. None of it accounts for the rand's move.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: An oil rally in early October forced out leveraged crypto bets: liquidations jumped 235% to $547 million, days after the US approved its first 3x leveraged funds. MARA, one of the largest miners, cut its holdings by 18,245 coins to fund AI computing. None of it explains the rise before that.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Two pulls cancelled out. The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act died in the US Senate and an oil rally forced $547 million of crypto liquidations, a 235% jump. Against that, the US approved its first 3x leveraged ether funds on 2 October, and traders shrugged off a $350 million theft from the exchange Bitget.

paxg.standing: The price of a troy ounce of gold, read from PAX Gold, a token backed by bars held in vaults. Gold pays no interest, so it trades against bond yields, and households and central banks hold it as savings.
paxg.recent: Gold slid despite a war, because rising oil prices came with a stronger US dollar and surging yields: markets price 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and a metal that pays no interest loses out as yields climb. India, the world's second-largest gold buyer, also confirmed banks have paid a 3% tax on imports since April.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: OpenAI scrapped the rollout of GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns, and a day later Trump and top tech firms signed a White House accord to self-police AI development. Then Anthropic's AI invented a tip on an unsolved Philadelphia killing, and Teen ChatGPT skipped crisis referrals in a quarter of tests. None of it falls on the day of the peak.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: The week's events ran from a plague-institute technician's death in Irkutsk, which Russian authorities put down to pneumonia and Trump said he would raise with Putin, to Ukrainian drones partly disabling two Yandex data centres and a US licence for Russian diesel. None of it falls on the days the series peaked or bottomed.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz in late September, and mediation between Iran and the US has since deadlocked. Projectiles then hit the tanker On Peace, injuring 12 crew, and another off Qatar; seven ships crossed on Tuesday, the fewest since 23 July. Iran says Oman has agreed coordinates for safe lanes.

wiki-india.standing: The number of times each day people open the Wikipedia article on India. It is a rough gauge of how much the world's most populous country is on readers' minds, and it jumps when one event breaks through.
wiki-india.recent: India's central bank raised its repo rate for the first time since 2023, police detained 260 people including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi at a New Delhi protest, and Musk accused Ambani of blocking Starlink. None of it accounts for the line on the chart.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Two months of attacks on tankers have emptied the lanes: Iran's Guards claimed a strike on a gas tanker in the strait, and projectiles hit another off Qatar. Mediation between Iran and the US deadlocked, then Tehran said Oman had agreed coordinates for safe lanes. The trade held back is Gulf oil and liquefied gas bound for Asia.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war has reached the strait's own shore. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces say they retook Mokha and secured Dhubab, cutting Houthi roads to Bab el-Mandeb, after blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha. The Houthis answered with missiles at Saudi forces and at Aden airport. None of it accounts for the earlier trough.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Most canal traffic also passes Bab al-Mandab, and the fight for that strait widened: Yemen said it retook Mocha and its army secured Dhubab beside the strait, Saudi Arabia planned an offensive against the Houthis, and two Saudi airports were targeted. None of it accounts for the swing in canal transits.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news was upstream of here, at Hormuz: projectiles hit tankers off Qatar and in the strait even as Middle East crude exports peaked at 22.5 million barrels daily on Kpler data. Those cargoes sail on to Asia, but none of it accounts for the traffic through this strait.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's news around the strait was military and political rather than maritime: Taipei received the first of its 66 ordered F-16V fighters, and the Philippines said it forced a Chinese survey ship from Batanes. Neither closed or rerouted a shipping lane, and nothing reported accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: A 7.7 earthquake toppled a tower in Penonomé and prompted tsunami warnings for neighbouring countries, but it struck after the last count shown here, and the reports do not say what happened to the canal. Nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the traffic.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones sank merchant ships in the Black Sea off Romania and Bulgaria, where the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan went down with its crew missing, and a crude tanker burned off Sochi with 23 Indian sailors rescued. Those attacks on the strait's grain and oil trade were reported after traffic had already thinned and do not account for the fall.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Blasts beside a tanker off Mokha, near Bab el-Mandeb, kept the Red Sea shortcut a risk, which is what sends ships around the Cape. The strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and off Qatar hit a different trade, crude and gas leaving by another route, and nothing reported accounts for the dip in traffic here in early September.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The war at sea reached shipping further down the Russian coast: a Ukrainian drone strike set a crude tanker ablaze off Sochi, 23 Indian sailors were rescued and New Delhi protested. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the empty strait itself.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia under the Mecca alliance as Houthis struck Riyadh and Aden, and Netanyahu ordered an ICC case against Erdogan. None of it is about Turkey's companies or its currency, and nothing reported in these weeks accounts for the fall in Istanbul shares.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, who faces a test of delivery on taking the job. Nothing reported in the fortnight ties that appointment, or anything else, to the index's path.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Japan's 10-year yield climbed to 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources said the Bank of Japan is considering declaring its 2% inflation goal reached. Both point to dearer borrowing for listed companies, and neither accounts for shares climbing.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The trough came as Europe's trade pressure on China peaked: Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access, and Brussels pressed Beijing over the yuan and a 360.6 billion euro deficit. A day later Beijing freed 550 billion yuan of unused local borrowing room and struck an interim deal with the EU limiting hybrid car exports.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Beijing let local governments tap 550 billion yuan of borrowing room that was already authorised and left idle, stimulus routed through the balance sheets it has spent years trying to shrink. The same week Brussels won a limit on China's hybrid car exports and pressed Beijing over the yuan. None of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Samsung guided to a quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, a first for any technology company, on demand for the memory chips that AI data centres consume. Seoul also spent the fortnight in rows with North Korea over a DMZ mine blast and with Ukraine. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India's central bank raised its repo rate to 5.5% on a 6-0 vote, the first rise since 2023, as trouble in Hormuz pushed up inflation risks, and dearer borrowing weighed on shares. Tata Consultancy Services then reported quarterly revenue up 11% on AI and international growth, lifting the IT sector.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's banks, the heaviest weight here, had been on a hot rally, and it stuttered as bond yields surged. The Treasury yield reached an 18-year high in late September, the same surge that sent gold to a 7-week low, and the pressure reached the lenders in the days that followed.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's Taiwan news was about security rather than business: the FBI arrested a woman accused of tracking the president's son, the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters landed in Taipei, and Trump denied asking Xi about US arms sales. None of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The trough came a day after annual inflation was reported at 4.0% for August, up from 3.5%, despite the rate hikes meant to slow it. The miners carry a slower worry: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports. Firmus then scrapped its Sydney listing after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's South African news was mostly off the trading floor: riots in Durban and Soweto over an asylum directive, and Durban's main terminal handling 30% less cargo after a mid-August software switch. Gold Fields had an A$39bn bid for Northern Star rejected. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% in the first round and leads into the 25 October runoff. His potential finance chief wants a fast fiscal policy fix, which bears on the Brazilian rates this market trades against, though he has also pledged pension rises above inflation.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Mexico's fortnight was Hurricane Polo making a 2nd landfall on the Pacific coast after Baja, a US troop deployment over a border shooting Mexico cannot verify, and a prison fight in Sinaloa. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The news out of Argentina in these weeks was about other things: Milei gave Britain 2 weeks to halt an oil project in the Falklands and threatened legal action over it, and the poverty rate climbed to over 32%. Neither accounts for the fall in share prices.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day oil pipeline to the Pacific, meant to diversify the economy away from the US. That bears directly on the energy producers that weigh so heavily in this index, but nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for its path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed in the United States, weighted by market value, on the largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The fortnight's US market news was about single names and appointments: Microsoft's shares fell 7.5% after Washington suspended it from the green card scheme, and Trump's stalled Fed pick Judy Shelton joined Treasury to advise on China. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The ECB raised rates in September and called the step proportionate after euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% from 3.2%, which keeps pressure on it to hike again and raises borrowing costs for German exporters. BMW put €2 billion into German plants while cutting jobs and warning on profit in China.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Schneider Electric lost nearly €15 billion in value on Monday after buying PTC, and France's central bank chief had to say the country needs no European Central Bank help yet. Macron and Merz sought power to cut off EU market access in a tougher stance on China, the market the index's luxury houses sell into.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The news from Amsterdam's companies ran against the index, not with it: Argenx's blockbuster Vyvgart failed to beat placebo in a Sjögren's trial, and BofA said a chip-technology move by ASML threatens Besi's shares. Neither accounts for the rise.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index's trough came days after Sánchez called an early election with Spain's Socialists trailing in polls. The vote followed a week of housing protests: tens of thousands marched after an 87-year-old's eviction, Congress rejected tenant protections, and police fired rubber bullets outside a property summit in Valencia.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italy's fortnight turned on fuel and bank ownership: truckers threatened a strike over €2.40 diesel, Azerbaijan's SOCAR capped pump prices across the country, and Unipol won ECB and Bank of Italy approval for de facto control of BPER Banca. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Swiss news of the past fortnight was political rather than corporate: a vote on writing neutrality into the constitution, the president's announcement that they will quit government, and five pacts signed with India on trade and professionals' mobility. None of it reaches the earnings of the handful of companies that carry the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: Flydubai suspended its Israel flights after a cockpit attack on a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight that Israeli authorities treated as a terror attack, and Israel ordered 20 British diplomats out of the country. Nothing reported ties either event to the slide in share prices.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Early October was crowded with his own decisions: sanctions that give the ICC six months, a panel convened to hear Lisa Cook, and a licence for 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel with the fuel at $6.32 a gallon. Democrats filed two suits saying he repurposed $20m meant for border commemorations. None of it accounts for the September peak.

wiki-united-states.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. The page is a standing reference for the country, so its surges mark the days American policy or power reached readers well beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: The peak came as reports said the Pentagon had drafted Iran strike options for use before 3 November, and as Washington barred Microsoft from the US green card scheme. A day later the US sanctioned the ICC, licensed Russian diesel, and Hegseth announced a 3 December firing-squad execution for Nidal Hasan.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end, with inflation above target for 5.5 years. The Labor Department counted 29,000 new jobs in September against 90,000 expected, so October is seen as a skip and markets price 80% odds of a December move. Trump has convened a panel on removing governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The European Central Bank raised rates in September, a step its officials called proportionate, as euro-zone inflation jumped to 3.8% that month from 3.2%, nearly double the target. Isabel Schnabel, the board's most influential voice for tighter policy, leaves on 3 January; governments have until 28 October to nominate a successor.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: The rise came with a payrolls report showing employers added just 29,000 jobs in September. Days later a NY Fed survey put short-term inflation expectations at a three-year high, so weak hiring and rising price expectations arrived together.

xag.standing: The price of an ounce of silver, read from KAG, a Kinesis token backed one-for-one by bullion. Silver is both a store of value and an industrial metal, so it moves with gold and with demand from solar panels and electronics.
xag.recent: The news in this window was about gold rather than silver: gold slid to a seven-week low as Treasury yields surged, oil rose and the US dollar strengthened, then touched a two-month low before recovering on a softer dollar. Silver trades in gold's wake, but nothing published names a cause of its own.

us-cpi.standing: The year-on-year change in the US consumer price index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what households pay for goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and dollar borrowing costs worldwide follow.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Tanker attacks kept shipping out of the strait: a projectile hit the tanker On Peace and injured 12 crew, another was struck 58 miles off Qatar, and Iran's Guards claimed a strike on a gas tanker. Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz and mediation deadlocked; Iran now says Oman agreed coordinates for safe lanes.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthis have seized territory at the entrance to the Red Sea since February, and the Yemeni army is now fighting to take it back: it retook Mocha and says it secured Dhubab, the district beside the strait. The Houthis say they fired on Saudi forces near the strait, and their missiles hit Riyadh's airport. None of it explains the container traffic.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The war is at the canal's southern approach: the Houthis have seized territory at the entrance to the Red Sea since February. Yemen says it has retaken Mocha, and its army that it secured Dhubab, beside Bab al-Mandab. Those advances came after the last reading here, and none of this accounts for the swings in traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: A 7.7 earthquake struck Panama and toppled a tower in Penonomé, but it came after the last reading on this chart, so the line does not show it. Nothing else from the past fortnight accounts for the canal's traffic.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight concerns this strait itself. The news upstream was Hormuz, where tankers were struck, Iran and Oman agreed safe lanes and crossings fell to a two-month low. Cargo from there bound for Asia passes through Malacca next, but nothing reported ties the two counts together.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily views of Wikipedia's article on Israel, a state at the centre of the Middle East's wars and diplomacy. The count jumps when an event sends people looking for background, marking when a story reached beyond the region.
wiki-israel.recent: A Flydubai co-pilot used a crash ax in an attempted cockpit takeover on a Dubai to Tel Aviv flight; UAE investigators called it a planned terrorist act and the airline suspended its Israel flights. A week later Israel ordered 20 British diplomats out and shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem. Neither falls on the late-September peak.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States launches a military invasion of Iran by its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each strike, threat and round of talks.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Reports that the Pentagon was drafting strike options before 3 November and that mediation had deadlocked pulled one way; Trump ruling out new attacks until after the midterms and Pezeshkian saying Iran will keep negotiating pulled the other. Strikes are also not an invasion, which is what this contract pays on.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Yemen's government launched an offensive on the Houthis, and its troops say they cut the group's roads to Bab el-Mandeb. The Houthis answered with missiles on Aden and Riyadh airports, killing at least 3 in Riyadh; Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying there. None of this explains the earlier peak.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia, the largest crude exporter and home to Islam's two holiest cities. Its output decisions move the oil price, and its wars and alliances reach across the Gulf and the Red Sea.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Yemen's Houthis hit two Saudi airports, then claimed a ballistic missile strike on Riyadh's airport, and Lufthansa and Air India stopped flying to the capital. The Mecca alliance activated collective deterrence, with Pakistan and Turkey sending troops. All of it came after the mid-September peak, which nothing here explains.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. The count jumps when the lab ships a model, loses staff or lands in a dispute, making it a gauge of public curiosity about AI.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI scrapped the rollout of a new model over safety concerns, then warned more than 100 organisations that its models may have entered their systems and fired two safety researchers and a program manager. Its safety-report lead David Robinson quit, and a release of more than 350 mathematical findings in one day followed.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: Central banks are tightening against an oil shock. India raised its repo rate to 5.5%, its first rise since 2023; the ECB defended its September hike with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, nearly double its target; and most Federal Reserve officials expect another rise by year-end. The IMF urged targeted cash over subsidies.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: A Russian guided bomb killed at least 30 bus passengers in Kramatorsk and a cruise missile killed 14 in a Pryluky apartment block. Zelenskyy said Washington won't help just as US envoys brought new plans, and Seoul recalled its Kyiv ambassador after a row over North Korean POWs. None of it accounts for the earlier September peak.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will be Israel's prime minister after the next government forms. The price is what traders pay for a yes share, and it moves on coalition arithmetic, polls and his court cases.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: A cockpit attack on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv left Israeli agencies trading blame over how the co-pilot was vetted, and Drop Site reported a CIA warning that Israel risks civil war. None of it bears on who forms the next government, and nothing reported accounts for the shift in the betting.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at a given meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each jobs and inflation release.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders moved toward a hold after the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs in September, against 90,000 expected, which undercut the case for an October hike. Most Fed officials still expect another rise by year-end, and Waller said there is some flexibility on its timing.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the Gulf terminal that loads the bulk of its crude exports. Traders are betting on a seizure or strike that would cut off most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: The Pentagon drafted Iran strike options, mediation between Iran and the US deadlocked, and Pezeshkian said Iran will keep negotiating. Trump then ruled out new attacks until after the November midterms. None of it concerned the island itself, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris becomes the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on polls, rival candidacies and her own stated plans.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A bet on whether Republicans hold a majority of the US House of Representatives after the 2026 midterm elections. All 435 seats are contested, and control decides which party can pass or block the president's legislation.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A New York crypto financial firm founded by Mike Novogratz that trades, lends and manages digital assets for institutions. It also owns a Texas data-centre campus leased for AI computing, so its share follows both bitcoin and AI demand.

stocks:NVO.standing: The Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy, and one of the world's largest makers of insulin. Its shares trade on demand for obesity and diabetes drugs, and on what insurers and governments will pay for them.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Traders paid more after Trump ruled out new attacks on Iran until after the November midterms and called talks with Tehran productive, while Pezeshkian said Iran will keep negotiating and Oman agreed coordinates for safe Hormuz lanes. That outweighed a deadlock in mediation, Pentagon strike options and a tanker strike claimed by Iran's Guards.

poly-will-jd-vance-win-the-2028-us-presi.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at $1 if JD Vance, the US vice-president, wins the 2028 presidential election. It prices the Republican succession years before any primary vote is cast.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio becomes the Republican presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a race where the sitting president cannot run again.

poly-will-david-lisnard-win-the-2027-fre.standing: What traders pay for a contract that settles in full if David Lisnard, the mayor of Cannes, wins France's 2027 presidential election. He is a free-market conservative in a crowded field on the French right.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every turn in the talks over the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Traders paid most for an early end while talks in New York were working through terms for reopening Hormuz. Trump then rejected Iran's proposal, mediation deadlocked, and the Pentagon drafted strike options before 3 November. Pezeshkian says Iran will keep negotiating, but the deadline is now days away.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-d-ho.standing: A contract that pays out if Republicans keep the US Senate and Democrats win the House in the 2026 midterms. That split leaves the Senate confirming the president's nominees while the House can block his bills.

stocks:UAL.standing: The parent of United Airlines, one of the three big US network carriers, with hubs including Chicago, Newark, Houston and San Francisco. Jet fuel is among its largest costs, so its shares move with oil prices and travel demand.

stocks:AXON.standing: The maker of the Taser and of the body cameras worn by most large American police forces, based in Scottsdale, Arizona. Its growth comes from the cloud subscriptions that store and manage the footage those cameras record.

poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran sign a final nuclear agreement before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for a yes share, so it moves with each report from the talks and the war around them.
poly-us-iran-final-nuclear-deal-by-decem.recent: Traders paid more for a deal as talks in New York turned to the terms for reopening Hormuz, then gave some back when Trump rejected Iran's proposal and mediation deadlocked. Since then the Pentagon drafted strike options, Trump ruled out new attacks until after the midterms, and Pezeshkian said Iran will keep negotiating.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still in force at its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every strike, threat or stalled talk in the Gulf.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Traders bet on the truce through a fortnight that tested it: Iran-US mediation deadlocked, the Pentagon drafted strike options and Iran's Guards claimed a tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz. Then Pezeshkian said Iran will keep negotiating and Trump ruled out new attacks until after the November midterms. None of it explains the earlier climb.

wiki-united-kingdom.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on the United Kingdom each day. It is a rough gauge of when the country draws the world's curiosity, and it jumps on elections, royal events and crises.
wiki-united-kingdom.recent: A suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, an airbase the US used for the Iran war, led to seven arrests, and Iran denied any link. The US then withdrew all 12 B-1 bombers, which Trump put down to terror threats, and Israel ordered 20 British diplomats out of East Jerusalem. None of it accounts for the earlier peak.

poly-will-texas-enact-a-data-center-mora.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Texas imposes a moratorium on new data centers before 2027. The state hosts one of the largest US build-outs of the facilities, and their power demand falls on its self-contained electricity grid.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback in late September, a commitment to retire its own stock that puts a standing buyer under the price. The same day it launched AI security tools meant to prevent agent breaches, a step beyond chips into software.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: A federal jury in San Diego awarded Taction Technology $5.72 billion from Apple in a haptics patent case just as the shares topped out. Days later Apple Pay launched in India on Axis Bank cards only, without UPI in a UPI-first market. Nothing reported accounts for the climb that came before.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon after months of delays and restricted it to trusted cyber defenders over safety concerns. The same day a judge in Washington dismissed the antitrust suits Chegg and Penske had brought against Google, and days later it signed up as buyer for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon built its 1,000th satellite and is weeks away from starting its space internet service. It also released new Kindles and Alexa tablets that drop the Fire branding before Prime Big Deal Days, then shuffled Alexa's leadership. None of that accounts for the share's move.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: The Trump administration suspended Microsoft and Adobe from the green card sponsorship scheme over fraud claims, and the shares fell 7.5% on the news. The same fortnight it unveiled a new AI Surface laptop, and contractors were reported to be reviewing images Copilot users upload. None of that accounts for the climb.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: A survey found licensing costs driving 90 percent of VMware users to explore options, a strain on the software side of the business rather than the chips. Nothing else reported in the fortnight bears on the company, and that alone does not account for the share price.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: Starship reached orbit for the first time in late September, even after losing one of its three main Raptor engines. A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile followed, and shares of Verizon and AT&T fell on it. In India, Starlink holds a licence but still cannot sell service.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses in late September and extended its Muse agent to small businesses, a line of income outside advertising. The same day a Santa Fe jury found it had deceived consumers 44 million times; a week later it rushed fixes for a Muse flaw that could have reached its internal databases.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: An 11-day pipeline shutdown stopped Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, and days after they resumed the Houthis said they had struck an oil facility near Riyadh while two tankers were hit in Hormuz. Saudi Arabia then unexpectedly cut its oil prices to Asia, and Aramco's CEO said replenishing lost supplies could take two years.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's third-quarter sales fell 2 percent, a result that landed as underwhelming. Its entry into India stalled alongside Starlink's, and Musk's courtship of the country ended in acrimony. Both came in October, so neither accounts for the July fall.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung forecast a third-quarter operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, a first for a technology company, on demand for the high-bandwidth memory AI data centres consume and a shortage that lifted ordinary DRAM and NAND prices too. The figure is preliminary guidance, and it arrived with a report that chip margins may be flat from here.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: Micron said memory demand will exceed supply for at least 2 years, and its CEO described supplies as only getting tighter. In a business where prices are set by scarcity, a shortage that long means the company sells every chip it makes at rising prices, with AI demand taking the output.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD agreed on Sep 28 to pay $8.2 billion for World Labs, the world models startup of AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li. That is a chip designer buying a company that builds AI models rather than the hardware they run on.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan in early October as part of a review of banks' private credit business, set off by worries about that market. Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley faced the same questions, so the scrutiny fell on the sector's largest lenders rather than on one bank alone.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix together control 83% of memory chips, which makes Korea the chokepoint for the memory that AI hardware depends on. That dominance held throughout the window, and nothing reported in it accounts for the fall in the share.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: ASML made a chip technology move that BofA says threatens the shares of Besi. Nothing else reported in the fortnight explains ASML's own price.

us-2y.standing: What the US government pays to borrow for two years. It follows the expected path of Federal Reserve interest rates more closely than any other Treasury yield, and the cost of short-term loans moves with it.
us-2y.recent: The one relevant headline of the fortnight asked what Washington does next if US bond yields keep rising. It treats the rise as given and names no cause for it.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in consumer prices across the countries that use the euro, as measured by Eurostat. The European Central Bank sets interest rates to hold it at 2%, so borrowing costs for the whole bloc follow it.
ez-cpi.recent: The September figure, published after this line ends, came in at 3.8%, the highest level in three years. That keeps pressure on the ECB to hike rates. The reports of the jump name no cause for it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: Alpenglow, an upgrade that cuts the time for a transaction to become final from 12.8 seconds to 150 milliseconds, reached its second public test network in late September. The Solana Foundation then launched DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds, and block times were scheduled to halve to 200 milliseconds this week.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The retreat from the late-September peak coincided with a hack at Bitget: the exchange paused withdrawals after $350 million was stolen, and the thief moved $83 million of XRP that Ripple cannot freeze. An XRP Ledger upgrade then slipped 10 days when validators reset its activation clock.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.
doge.recent: Dogecoin got an Ethereum-style testnet for trading, lending and stablecoins at the start of October, a step toward giving the coin uses beyond speculation. It arrived after the swings on the chart and does not account for them; Bitcoin's soft-inflation pop faded the same day as bond yields refused to fall.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Researchers published a 'Shielded Bitcoin' paper proposing Zcash-style private payments for Bitcoin without a fork. Days later developers released Udon, moving Tachyon scaling code into the network's shared cryptography library, and 25-second blocks went live on public testnet ahead of schedule after Gemini switched software to prepare.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.
link.recent: The peak came a day after Chainlink launched CCIP 2.0, an upgrade that gives big crypto apps more control over their own security. Nothing else in the window's news accounts for the earlier trough or the retreat that followed.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: For a decade the Bank of Japan held rates near zero on the argument that underlying inflation was still short of its 2% target. Three sources told Reuters the bank is weighing saying this month that the target is roughly met, which removes its own stated reason to hold. Oil prices since the war on Iran have raised Japanese import costs.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The fortnight's argument was about China's currency, not its rate. The EU pressed Beijing over a ballooning trade deficit and charges of yuan manipulation, and the PBOC backed its FX policy as the yuan hit a four-year high against its basket. None of it touched the policy rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's own news this fortnight was about its balance sheet, not its policy: international reserves fell 4.85% in September to $731.76 bln, and it made no yuan purchases or sales in early October. None of that accounts for the rate.

wiki-petroleum.standing: The crude oil pumped from underground and refined into petrol, diesel, jet fuel and the feedstock for plastics. It is the world's most traded commodity, and its price runs through transport, food and inflation everywhere.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Aramco says almost 3 billion barrels of supply were lost while Hormuz was shut, and that refilling stocks could take two years. OPEC+ kept November quotas unchanged, Iraq began trucking crude through Syria, and the US pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks. Iran and Oman have since agreed a 'safe route' through the strait.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-texas-se.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins the US Senate seat Texas fills in 2026. Texas has not elected a Democrat statewide since 1994, so the price tracks how far the national map has moved.

poly-will-aleksandar-vucic-united-serbia.standing: What traders will pay for a share that pays out if the Serbian Progressive Party, the party built around President Aleksandar Vučić, wins the most seats in Serbia's parliamentary election. It has governed since 2012.

poly-will-alberto-nunez-feijoo-be-the-ne.standing: What traders pay for a contract that settles in full if Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of Spain's conservative People's Party, is the next prime minister. It moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and election timing.

stocks:DAL.standing: One of the three largest US airlines, flying from hubs including Atlanta, Detroit and Minneapolis. Its share price moves on jet fuel costs and on demand for business and premium travel, and it reports results before its rivals.
stocks:DAL.recent: Delta cut its profit outlook after saying fuel will cost it $6 billion more this year, even with demand for seats holding strong. That is a squeeze on margins rather than on sales, and it arrived at the very end of the window, so it does not account for the share's earlier climb.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential runoff by a margin of less than four percentage points. Its price is what traders will pay for a narrow win, not a forecast of one.
poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.recent: Brazil voted on 4 October for a president, governors and lawmakers, and the presidential race went to a runoff after a strong showing by Bolsonaro that left the left on the ropes. Nothing reported since the first round accounts for traders abandoning the narrow-margin bet.

stocks:LLY.standing: An Indianapolis drugmaker whose tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, made it the world's most valuable pharmaceutical company. Its share moves on demand, pricing and supply of that one drug class.

stocks:LHA.DE.standing: Germany's largest airline group, owner of Swiss, Austrian Airlines, Brussels Airlines and Eurowings. Its profits turn on jet fuel costs, long-haul business travel and wage deals with pilots and cabin crew, whose strikes ground it.
stocks:LHA.DE.recent: Lufthansa stopped flying to Riyadh, as did Air India, after a Houthi attack on the airport there killed 3 people in Saudi Arabia. One suspended route is a small piece of the network, and it came at the end of a slide that was already weeks old; nothing else reported in the period accounts for the share.

stocks:MARA.standing: One of the largest listed bitcoin miners, running power-hungry data centres that earn new coins and keeping a large reserve of them. Its share tends to move with the bitcoin price, amplified by what its power costs.
stocks:MARA.recent: MARA has been selling the bitcoin it used to accumulate: holdings fell by 18,245 coins between February and August to pay down debt and build AI computing infrastructure. This week about 996 BTC, worth $81.1 million, moved to an address a chain-analytics firm identified as Galaxy Digital's.

stocks:KEL.KA.standing: The private utility that generates, transmits and distributes electricity to Karachi, Pakistan's largest city, listed on the Pakistan Stock Exchange. Its plants burn imported gas, and a state regulator sets what it may charge.
stocks:KEL.KA.recent: The utility is short of re-gasified liquefied natural gas: cargoes are late because of disruption to global supply, and it warned it may cut power at evening and night peaks as an extreme, last-resort measure. No cuts have been ordered. The warning came after the share's slide and does not by itself account for it.

poly-will-apple-be-the-largest-company-i.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Apple is the world's most valuable listed company at the close on December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set against rivals such as Nvidia and Microsoft.

stocks:CSCO.standing: A San Jose maker of the routers, switches and security software that carry corporate and internet traffic. Its orders are read as a gauge of how much businesses and telecom carriers are spending on networks.
stocks:CSCO.recent: 10 countries signed trade deals with Washington that limit which telecom suppliers they may buy from. Terms like these decide who is allowed to sell network equipment in those markets, which is the business this company is in.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether commercial shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait joining the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, is effectively halted by the deadline. The strait carries Suez-bound trade between Asia and Europe.

poly-will-the-price-of-bitcoin-be-betwee.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Bitcoin's price sits between $82,000 and $84,000 on October 10. Its price is what traders will pay for that one narrow outcome, so it swings hard as the deadline nears and the range of possible prices shrinks.

stocks:LMT.standing: The world's largest defence contractor by revenue and the maker of the F-35 fighter. Most of its sales come from the US government, so its share moves on Pentagon budgets and on foreign arms orders.
stocks:LMT.recent: Taiwan took delivery of the first 2 of the 66 F-16V fighters it ordered, and the US Navy set out plans to arm B-52 bombers with the stealthy AGM-158C anti-ship missile. Both are the company's products, and both are deliveries and plans on existing programmes; neither accounts for the share's slide.

poly-putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before its deadline, for any reason. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome; it moves on the war and on strain in Moscow.
poly-putin-out-as-president-of-russia-by.recent: Traders paid less for an exit as Putin set terms rather than faced them: he ruled out a long-range strike ceasefire, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed energy talks with US negotiators. Ukraine's 650-drone attack on Moscow and its strikes on Yandex data centres did not shift the betting.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The trough came days after Bangkok was declared a flood disaster zone: almost 300mm of rain fell, the worst floods in 15 years stranded residents, and Thailand gave the civil service a two-day holiday. The shutdown landed on the city where the exchange itself trades.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's airport on consecutive days, killing at least 3, after the group warned that Saudi airspace would become a theatre of military operations. The war in Yemen had reached the capital where these shares trade, and Pakistan and Turkey agreed to send troops to the kingdom.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: A flydubai co-pilot tried to seize a Dubai–Tel Aviv flight with a crash ax, the UAE called it terrorism, and the airline suspended its Israel flights. Days later only seven ships crossed Hormuz in a day, the fewest since 23 July. Both strike at the travel and trade Dubai lives on.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
